rules.ask: Does this verified package cycle contain a dependency on a separable responsibility whose relocation would remove a specific edge of the shown cycle?
rules.subject: block
rules.nextCheck: Follow the return import in the cycle witness. Check whether it runs in production, then move or inject the referenced responsibility on paper and trace whether the same dependency remains.

rules.ask: Do separate changes repeatedly require these packages to update independent copies of the same policy in lockstep?
rules.subject: block
rules.nextCheck: Read the two package patches side by side in each cited commit. Identify the behavior that would diverge if one side were reverted, and check whether it recurs outside release or formatting changes.

rules.ask: Does the required interface force the shown client or its provider to supply an operation for another role that its own job cannot meaningfully implement?
rules.subject: block
rules.nextCheck: Trace the required member from the consumer to the provider stub. Try a type containing only the operations this role calls and check whether another promised operation breaks.

rules.ask: Can a caller following the shared contract observe a broken guarantee when it substitutes the shown implementation?
rules.subject: block
rules.nextCheck: Replay the same contract-valid input on both implementations. Compare the promised result or error, including the documented environment and any allowed variation.

rules.ask: Does a consumer encode knowledge of a changeable internal design decision such that replacing the representation while preserving the intended operation would force that consumer to change?
rules.subject: block
rules.nextCheck: Look up the consumer-facing type that declares the accessed keys or operations. If it promises those exact names and meanings, dismiss the layout warning. Otherwise substitute an accessor for the backing object and identify which consumer expression would break while the documented behavior stays the same.
